Senses.Explanation: Being capable of giving rise to the myriad phenomena is equated in the cited formula with the nature of phenomena and also with the nature-body; another exchange asks directly what can give rise to them. Three witnesses transmit the sequence: knowing nature is called knowing-nature; what can give rise to the myriad things is called the nature of things, also named the nature-body. A fourth asks directly what it is that can give rise to the myriad things. None names Huineng or presents the separate self-nature declaration.
